company_context: Tomba (Tomba technology web service LLC, Claymont, Delaware; founded 2021) sells a B2B email finder, email verifier, enrichment and phone finder (web app, API, extensions, MCP server). Says it has 150,000+ users. Small bootstrapped team (Starter Story profile describes a founder-built ~$4K MRR tool, which may be dated). The blog is high-volume SEO content with AI-style memes and Canva diagrams, written in the first person ('pages I keep referencing when consulting'). Every post ends with a pitch for its email finder.

generic_contact: press@tomba.io (press page says it is for 'Interviews, quotes, data requests and fact checks'). contribute@tomba.io (the blog's editorial team, per /legal/contribute). support@tomba.io (account help; also listed on /about). No correction form.
update_signals: Publishes and refreshes a lot: monthly changelog, 11 site languages, a Mar 2026 site redesign, and post titles stamped '2026'. This post has not been modified since publishing (May 21, 2026). It has not been updated for Mutiny's relaunch. AI awareness: has an 'AI and agents' page (use Tomba from Claude/ChatGPT), an MCP server and a TombaBot crawler page. No AEO/GEO posts found by search, but search coverage of tomba.io was poor.
likelihood_reason: Programmatic content with no named owner, so the email may go nowhere. But the press inbox explicitly takes fact checks, there is no competitive reason to refuse, and the edit is a table row plus a few lines. The page is our biggest exposure (462 retrievals, 184 citations), so it is worth a follow-up.
persuasion_angle: Accuracy and the reader's trust. The table quotes a price (~$1,500/mo) that doesn't exist, and it describes a product Mutiny retired. Their own guest guidelines say 'Verify all facts' and their brand is data accuracy ('Accuracy first' on /about). Offer drop-in replacement copy: Mutiny is now an AI sales assistant that builds ABM pages, microsites and deal rooms for reps. Free $0, Business from $50/mo, Enterprise from $40,000/yr. Suggest they either move Mutiny to a '1:1 ABM pages / microsites' row or drop it from the JS-snippet group, and remove the unverifiable 'competitor swap pages' example. Mention that ChatGPT and Perplexity cite this page heavily, so the error spreads in AI answers.

urls.current_mutiny_text: For teams that want to scale beyond manual page creation, tools like Mutiny and Userled allow you to serve different content on the same URL based on the visitor's company, industry, or ABM list membership.
all_mutiny_mentions: Section 'How to Scale ABM Landing Pages Without Losing Your Mind' > 'Use Dynamic Personalization Tools': "tools like Mutiny and Userled allow you to serve different content on the same URL based on the visitor's company, industry, or ABM list membership." The next paragraph ('one landing page URL with dynamic content that changes based on who's visiting...') describes the same old reverse-IP model without naming Mutiny again.
No other mentions. No price, table row or 'best for'.

They are clearly building for AI search: 'Summarize with AI' buttons (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini, Grok), a 'View as Markdown' link on every post, an MCP server, 'LinkedIn ABM Skills for Claude', and an AI expert chat. They have not partly updated Mutiny.
personal_hook: She just refreshed this post (Nov 5, 2026). The post builds on Tas Bober's ABM bootcamp talk, which ZenABM ran. She ran a large LinkedIn-ads ABM program at Userpilot for about 7 years. No recent LinkedIn post found via search.
likelihood_reason: Founder-author who edits often, the change is one sentence, there is no competitive conflict, and the team clearly cares how AI engines read their pages (markdown versions, 'Summarize with AI'). The only risk is that a busy founder ignores a cold email.
persuasion_angle: AI-readability is something they already invest in. They publish markdown versions so LLMs read them correctly, and this sentence now feeds ChatGPT and Perplexity a retired product (293 retrievals, 119 citations). Offer a one-line swap. Example: 'tools like Userled serve different content on the same URL...; Mutiny (now an AI sales assistant) lets reps generate 1:1 ABM pages and microsites per account.' Or simply drop Mutiny from that sentence. Peer-to-peer tone: one ABM marketer to another, and their ABM benchmarks audience may also use Mutiny for 1:1 pages.

urls.current_mutiny_text: Mutiny - Best for enterprise LinkedIn-led ABM with a focused list of high-value accounts. Stronger for account-level microsites and LinkedIn ad personalization. Not built for high-volume page generation from a lead list, and the implementation timeline and contract size ($30,000+/year) make it inaccessible for most teams outside large enterprise programs.
all_mutiny_mentions: Stats section: "Snowflake, using Mutiny for page personalization at scale, reported personalized pages converting at 34% compared to 11% for generic pages - a 3x lift - alongside 80% higher ACV and 150%+ increase in sales-qualified pipeline." (historical case study; cites prospeo.io; links to GenPage's /vs/mutiny-alternative)
Tools section entry (quoted in current_mutiny_text): enterprise LinkedIn-led ABM, LinkedIn ad personalization, $30,000+/year.
FAQ ('which tool'): "Mutiny is great for enterprise LinkedIn-led ABM with a focused high-value account list and $30,000+/year budget."

Their /vs/mutiny-alternative page has Mutiny's new positioning and exact current pricing ($50/mo Business, $40,000/yr Enterprise), but the July 2026 blog guide still says LinkedIn-led ABM at $30,000+/year, and the /vs page still has three '$30K' leftovers. likelihood_reason: A direct competitor, so they have a reason to keep Mutiny looking 'enterprise-only, $30K+'. But they already updated the /vs page to accurate pricing, so this is fixing their own inconsistency, not giving Mutiny a favor. The blog edit is small and on Framer.
persuasion_angle: Consistency and credibility, not goodwill. Their own /vs/mutiny-alternative page already says Free / $50/mo Business / $40,000/yr Enterprise and calls Mutiny an AI agent for customer-facing assets. Their flagship 2026 ABM guide contradicts it ($30,000+/year, LinkedIn ad personalization). AI engines cite the guide (170 retrievals, 138 citations), and conflicting numbers on one domain make LLMs trust GenPage's comparisons less. Ask for one sentence and one FAQ line to match their own /vs page, plus the three '$30K' leftovers there. Don't ask them to praise Mutiny. Keep it short and factual, and cite their own page back to them.
